observations.seen: Frame 1 is lit flat and grey with almost no key direction, so players read as cutouts. Frame 2 has a warm low sun with long shadows and the strongest mood. Frame 4 has an indoor ambient look but no clear overhead flood key on the court.

Frame 2's long shadows have visible stair-step aliasing along the bleacher and court edges, which points to a low shadow-map resolution. Frames 1 and 3 show only faint blob contact shadows under the feet, so players look like they float.
Frame 4's glossy floor reflects the players and the red key, which works. Frames 1 to 3 have matte floors with no environment reflection, and the ball and skin show no specular response.

Frames 1 and 2 use extruded box buildings with repeated window grids and no detail. Frame 3 has a palm tree floating unattached in the sky and a pale slab horizon. Frame 4 uses a blurred photo backplate that does not match the 3D court's perspective.

Frame 3 has pink distance haze. Frame 4 has sparse dust particles near the hoop. Frames 1 and 2 have no haze or depth fade, and none of the frames shows the indoor haze over the court that the recipe expects.

Clothing, skin, and the court surface are flat colour with no roughness variation, fabric detail, or wear. Court lines in frame 1 are plain white strips, and the backboard art is the only textured surface.

Characters are low-poly with blocky hands and hair cards, and they are near-identical proportionally. The ball cart and the hoop with its net are the most detailed assets. The bleachers are plain stepped boxes.
The hoop is cropped at the top-right corner and one player is cut off at the right edge. The bottom third is empty floor, and the court fills about 70% of the frame, far above the 25–40% target.
The camera is a low perspective three-quarter view, roughly 20–25° down, not the elevated 70° orthographic broadcast view. The same fixed framing repeats in every frame.
Frame 4 has depth of field, bloom, and a vignette, which add polish. Frame 1 has no visible grading. Frame 2's warm grade works, but the treatment varies a lot from frame to frame.

The ball handler's dribble poses change across frames. Every other player holds the same stiff arms-out idle pose in every frame, and the white swoosh markers at their feet look like placeholder motion cues.

The only UI is an orange selection ring under the ball handler and white arcs at the feet. There is no score, clock, or possession indicator. Pixel-font text is painted on the floor in frames 3 and 4.
